title: Expansion of an iterated Tate-source datum
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-pur-conventions]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$. For a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $G_T=Lg_{T,\gamma}^*$, with $g_{T,\gamma}=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius $\gamma$ [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius]. Work on the small pro-etale derived categories with $A=A_{E,n}$ and the operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $X_0\xrightarrow{f_0}Y_0\xrightarrow{h_0}Z_0$ be separated finite-type morphisms between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes whose geometric base changes $f,h$ are smooth of pure relative dimensions $d,e\ge0$. For $s=f,h,hf$ set $P_sM=Ls^*M(r_s)[2r_s]$, with $r_f=d$, $r_h=e$, $r_{hf}=d+e$. Use the source-arrow construction $b_{s,M}$ and the strict datum of [def-pur-tate-datum], with the canonical Tate arrows [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ have datum $\varphi:G_ZK\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. Give $P_hK$ the arrow $\psi_h=(Lh^*\varphi\otimes\tau_{e,Y})[2e]b_{h,K}$ and give $P_fP_hK$ the iterated arrow $\psi_{f,h}=(Lf^*\psi_h\otimes\tau_{d,X})[2d]b_{f,P_hK}$. Let
$$a_{f,h,d,e,K}:P_{hf}K\xrightarrow{\sim}P_fP_hK$$
be the canonical comparison of [def-pur-composition-comparisons], characterized by its pullback-composition, tensor-pullback, ordered twist-power, associativity, and shift-reassociation factors, and put $J=a_{f,h,d,e,K}^{-1}:P_fP_hK\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{hf}K$. Then
$$J\psi_{f,h}=\bigl(L(hf)^*\varphi\otimes\tau_{d+e,X}\bigr)[2(d+e)]b_{hf,K}G_X(J).$$
In the unshifted expansion the three arrow factors are $L(hf)^*\varphi$, $Lf^*\tau_{e,Y}$, and $\tau_{d,X}$; the last two identify with $\tau_{d+e,X}$. The initial comparison identifies with $b_{hf,K}$, and all shift and degree-zero twist symmetries in $J$ have sign $1$. These assertions include $d=0$ and $e=0$ with the coefficient unit.

proof.text: Put $F_s=Ls^*$, $T_{r,V}=A_V(r)$ and $N=2(d+e)$. Expand $P_fP_hK$ as $R=(F_fF_hK\otimes F_fT_{e,Y}\otimes T_{d,X})[N]$, with the order of factors shown. Write $j:R\to P_{hf}K$ for $J$ in these coordinates. Substituting the two defining datum formulas, functoriality and naturality of the pullback-tensor comparison give an initial map $B:G_X(P_fP_hK)\to Q$, where $Q=(F_fF_hG_ZK\otimes G_XF_fT_{e,Y}\otimes G_XT_{d,X})[N]$, followed by the map $a:Q\to R$ whose factors are $F_fF_h\varphi$, $F_f\tau_{e,Y}\circ c_{f,T_{e,Y}}$, and $\tau_{d,X}$. Here $c_f:G_XF_f\to F_fG_Y$ is the commuting-pullback comparison. Thus $J\psi_{f,h}=jaB$. This is substitution of the displayed source-datum composite, using naturality for the actual derived morphism $\varphi$, rather than choosing a chain representative for it.

proof.text: Let $U=F_fT_{e,Y}$ and $t=t_{f,e}:U\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{e,X}$. Put $u=\alpha_{e,d,X}(t\otimes1):U\otimes^LT_{d,X}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{d+e,X}$, identifying $e+d=d+e$. Define $C:Q\to(F_{hf}G_ZK\otimes G_XT_{d+e,X})[N]$ by the pullback compositor on the first factor and $G_X(u)\mu_{g_X;U,T_{d,X}}^{-1}$ on the last two factors. The composition clause of [lem-pur-finite-tate-source-structural-coherence], applied to the given $f,h,K$, says precisely $CB=b_{hf,K}G_X(J)$: its first expansion is $B$, and its second expansion is $b_{hf,K}$ followed by the identifications inverse to $C$. This identifies the initial comparison, with the same shift identifications and specified canonical pullback compositors.

proof.text: Write $\beta=F_f(\tau_{e,Y})c_{f,T_{e,Y}}:G_XU\to U$. The pullback equation of [lem-pur-canonical-tate-arrow-naturality], with $w=f,r=e$, gives $t\beta=\tau_{e,X}G_X(t)$, since $c_f=C_f^{-1}$ in that lemma's notation. Its additivity equation with $r=e,s=d$ is $\alpha_{e,d,X}(\tau_{e,X}\otimes\tau_{d,X})\mu_{g_X;T_{e,X},T_{d,X}}=\tau_{d+e,X}G_X(\alpha_{e,d,X})$. Substitute the first equation into the second, using naturality of $\mu$ under $t\otimes1$ from [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], and compose with $\mu_{g_X;U,T_{d,X}}^{-1}$. This gives the typed identity $u(\beta\otimes\tau_{d,X})=\tau_{d+e,X}G_X(u)\mu_{g_X;U,T_{d,X}}^{-1}$. Naturality of the isomorphism of functors in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] changes $F_fF_h\varphi$ into $F_{hf}\varphi$; naturality of $\mu$ separates this factor from the twist factors. Thus $ja=(F_{hf}\varphi\otimes\tau_{d+e,X})[N]C$. Compose with $B$ and use Step 2 to obtain the required equality and the three unshifted factors.

proof.text: The Tate-arrow lemma explicitly supplies the degree-zero twist and even-shift sign convention and the coefficient-unit case. In the displayed expansion only degree-zero Tate factors pass the shifts $[2d]$ and $[2e]$; the possible shift-interchange scalar is $(-1)^{(2d)(2e)}=1$. Thus every symmetry used in $J$ has sign $1$. If $d=0$ or $e=0$, replace the corresponding Tate line by $A$ and its arrow by the coefficient-unit arrow; the same equations use the corresponding unitors and $[0]$. They still give the asserted formula, including $d=e=0$.

statement_change.what: The original statement described J as an informal composite of pullback, tensor, twist, and shift comparisons, but the Lean declaration uses the already-defined canonical comparison compositionSourceIdentification. Its ownership and normalization are the notion of def-pur-composition-comparisons; without citing that node, the recorded stmt_deps did not justify the J used by the Lean statement. The correction names a_{f,h,d,e,K} from that definition and sets J to its inverse, while retaining the source arrow identity and all edge cases.
